title: Chapter 97: The Rampaging Pen Spirit
html:
“This room feels different,” Zhu Jianing said from the doorway, poised to flee at any moment. “It feels like an escape room. The clues to the exit are probably hidden here, right?”

“No idea. I’ve never visited a Haunted House that gave its guests so much freedom. The owner must be very confident no one will get hurt.” Fei Youliang approached the chairs and picked up a sheet of paper. It read, “When will I die? How will I die? Who will die next?”

“This looks like the Pen Spirit game, but…” Fei Youliang eyed the ballpoint pen on the chair. “What happened to that pen?”

“Does it hide some kind of mechanism?” Zhu Jianing took the pen and clicked it several times, nearly snapping it. “Seems normal to me.”

“Do you still remember what the Haunted House boss said before we came in?”

“There are four scenarios in the Haunted House, and we have to experience them all before we can get the clues to the exit.”

“Right. The clues are hidden in these four areas. Let’s search carefully. In my experience, there’s probably a key or note hidden in this room.”

The bedroom was small, and the pair searched every corner but came up with nothing.

“This Haunted House won’t be easy to solve. The design is incredibly detailed.” Fei Youliang set the papers on the chair. Three bore writing; one was blank. “Do we have to play the Pen Spirit game before we get our clue?”

“Playing the Pen Spirit game inside a Haunted House sounds like a terrible idea.” The questions on the paper had rattled Zhu Jianing.

“Of the four scenarios, this one seems the simplest. If you don’t want to do this, we’ll need to go back to that classroom. Would you prefer that?” Fei Youliang waved his hand impatiently. “Plus, do you really think there is a Pen Spirit in this world? Get over here. We’ll try it once, and if it doesn’t work, we’ll leave.”

Something felt wrong. An inexplicable pressure tightened around Fei Youliang’s heart. Reluctantly, Zhu Jianing took his place across the chairs.

“But I don’t know how the game works.”

“Don’t worry. I’ve seen plenty of Pen Spirit movies, and I’ve even tried the ritual at home. It’s only a trick with a scientific explanation.” Fei Youliang held the pen above the blank sheet. “Cross your fingers over mine and grip the pen tightly.”

“Okay.” Zhu Jianing squatted down beside the chair and did what he was told. “Now what?”

“Just be quiet.” Fei Youliang wrote down “YES” and “NO” on the white paper. When the bedroom became completely quiet, he started to chant, “Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, you are my spirit from my previous life, and I am your spirit in this life. If you are with us, please draw a circle on the paper.”

As the invocation ended, a cold gust rattled the half-open bedroom door. The dilapidated panel swung wide, revealing the empty, dim corridor. Zhu Jianing shivered and instinctively shrank farther into the room.

“Don’t move.” Fei Youliang stared at the pen tip, rigid as a statue. Icy wind streamed through the room. Papers fluttered across the floor as though an invisible hand were turning them. The temperature fell, and cold seeped upward from their ankles.

Holding the same position under such strain sharpened every sensation until the ritual became a form of torture.

The decrepit bedroom darkened. A filthy sheet stirred in the wind as though something beneath the bed were crawling free. After ten minutes, their suspended hands began to tremble, stippling the paper with ink.

Zhu Jianing could not help but ask, “Has the Pen Spirit arrived?”

He could no longer bear the tension.

“Movies say the Pen Spirit appears after ten minutes, and if nothing happens by then, the game has failed. That rule is completely invented. People think the spirit has arrived, but it’s only a psychological effect,” Fei Youliang said, trying to calm his companion. “This is one of the four scenarios the owner mentioned. We’ll follow his rules and see what trick he tries.”

The moment he finished, the ballpoint pen twitched between their hands. The movement was slight, but both men felt it.

“Was that you?” they asked in unison, each seeing his own shock reflected on the other’s face.

“It wasn’t me,” Zhu Jianing blurted. He had barely recovered from the eyes in the drawer, and now his nerves stretched to the breaking point. “Youliang, do you think the real Pen Spirit came?”

“Don’t be ridiculous. The ritual and environment create psychological pressure. Holding one position for so long makes the pen seem to move by itself, when it’s really our bodies responding to stress and fatigue,” Fei Youliang explained, sounding as though he were convincing himself. “The subconscious expects movement, and the conscious mind interprets it as real.”

The pen moved again, far more distinctly this time. The pair exchanged a look, then turned to the paper. A line had joined the scattered ink dots into an irregular circle.

“F*ck! It’s really here!” Zhu Jianing’s first reaction was to pull his hand back, but he was stopped by Fei Youliang.

“Whether or not it is the real Pen Spirit, we have to continue this game.”

“Why?”

“If it’s real and we stop without dismissing it, the spirit will curse us until we die. If it’s fake, there’s nothing to fear—it’s only another trick arranged by the owner.”

“Then what shall we do next?”

“Try to ask it some questions, and then send the Pen Spirit away,” Fei Youliang said calmly.

“What should we ask? Something like the questions on those papers?” Zhu Jianing pointed to the sheets scattered across the floor.

“That’s a trap. Never ask the Pen Spirit about death. We’ll choose something harmless.”

“Random questions?”

“I’ll try.” Fei Youliang tightened his grip on Zhu Jianing’s hand. After shushing him, he murmured, “Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, can you tell me the name of my future wife?”

The moment he finished, the wind died. An unbearable pressure swelled behind him.

The pen in their hands quivered violently, and soon, three words appeared on the white paper.

“YOU WILL DIE!”
